name: Bill Hagerty

issue_poll.name: Gallup, U.S. registered voters, Oct 1-19, 2026 - share rating each issue 'extremely important' to their midterm vote
issue_poll.note: National fallback: no 2026 Tennessee poll ranking a full set of issues for all voters was found. Tennessee polls that exist agree on the top: Cygnal (Mar 16-17, 2026, likely GOP primary voters) ranked cost of living/inflation 24%, immigration 15%, jobs/economy 10% (https://www.cygn.al/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/TN-GOP-Primary-Gov-Poll-Memo.pdf); the Vanderbilt Poll (Apr 13-29, 2026, n=1,203 registered voters) found 88% call the cost of living expensive (https://news.vanderbilt.edu/2026/05/20/vanderbilt-poll-tennesseans-continue-to-express-anxiety-about-the-economy/). Gallup order used as is: economy 50%, health care 50%, Iran 47%, income and wealth distribution 44%, gas prices 42%, immigration 40%, abortion 38%, crime 35%, Israeli-Palestinian conflict 35%, AI data center construction 30%. Climate change (29%) fell to 11th. Economy merged with cost of living given Tennessee polling.

issues.detail: Pass Freedom to Build Act (S. 4265): HUD grant priority for localities that ease housing construction rules; cut federal spending
Expand health savings accounts; increase health care price transparency; cut fraud in health programs
Support the administration's Iran MOU; no financial relief to Iran until it takes required compliance steps
Energy independence and more energy production; no specific measure
Fund ICE and Border Patrol through budget reconciliation; border security
Uphold the rule of law; no specific measure
Hamas removed from power and hostages released; Gaza food aid via Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, not UNRWA

plan_caveats: Issue ranking is national (Gallup, Oct 2026); no full 2026 Tennessee issue ranking was found, only partial state results.
Hagerty ran a low-profile campaign: no 2026 issue pages found (teamhagerty.com shows 2020-era content), no debate, and he skipped the Ballotpedia and iVoterGuide questionnaires.

Most Concrete/Partial ratings come from Senate-office releases and Fox appearances made while a declared 2026 candidate (Aug 2025-Jun 2026), counted as forward-looking statements, not record; stricter reading would downgrade them.

Economy rated Concrete because Hagerty introduced and promoted the named Freedom to Build Act in April 2026 and pledged on election night to make homeownership more affordable; the bill links to cost of living only through housing.
Health care (Dec 2025) and Israel (Aug 2025) statements predate the 2026 calendar year.
Task cites CBS News projection; sources found credit the AP (call at 10:31 p.m. CDT, Nov 3); early returns about 54% to Bradshaw's 44%.
Abortion, income inequality and AI data centers: searched, no 2026 statements found.
